per_entity.label: ActivityInfluence
per_entity.definition: ActivityInfluence provides additional descriptions of an Activity's binary influence upon any other kind of resource. Instances of ActivityInfluence use the prov:activity property to cite the influencing Activity.

per_entity.label: AgentInfluence
per_entity.definition: AgentInfluence provides additional descriptions of an Agent's binary influence upon any other kind of resource. Instances of AgentInfluence use the prov:agent property to cite the influencing Agent.

per_entity.label: Association
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Association provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasAssociatedWith relation from an prov:Activity to some prov:Agent that had some responsiblity for it. For example, :baking prov:wasAssociatedWith :baker; prov:qualifiedAssociation [ a prov:Association; prov:agent :baker; :foo :bar ].

per_entity.label: Attribution
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Attribution provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasAttributedTo relation from an prov:Entity to some prov:Agent that had some responsible for it. For example, :cake prov:wasAttributedTo :baker; prov:qualifiedAttribution [ a prov:Attribution; prov:entity :baker; :foo :bar ].

per_entity.label: Bundle
per_entity.definition: Note that there are kinds of bundles (e.g. handwritten letters, audio recordings, etc.) that are not expressed in PROV-O, but can be still be described by PROV-O.

per_entity.label: Communication
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Communication provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasInformedBy relation from an informed prov:Activity to the prov:Activity that informed it. For example, :you_jumping_off_bridge prov:wasInformedBy :everyone_else_jumping_off_bridge; prov:qualifiedCommunication [ a prov:Communication; prov:activity :everyone_else_jumping_off_bridge; :foo :bar ].

per_entity.label: Delegation
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Delegation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:actedOnBehalfOf relation from a performing prov:Agent to some prov:Agent for whom it was performed. For example, :mixing prov:wasAssociatedWith :toddler . :toddler prov:actedOnBehalfOf :mother; prov:qualifiedDelegation [ a prov:Delegation; prov:entity :mother; :foo :bar ].

per_entity.label: Derivation
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Derivation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasDerivedFrom relation from some derived prov:Entity to another prov:Entity from which it was derived. For example, :chewed_bubble_gum prov:wasDerivedFrom :unwrapped_bubble_gum; prov:qualifiedDerivation [ a prov:Derivation; prov:entity :unwrapped_bubble_gum; :foo :bar ].

per_entity.label: End
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:End provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasEndedBy relation from some ended prov:Activity to an prov:Entity that ended it. For example, :ball_game prov:wasEndedBy :buzzer; prov:qualifiedEnd [ a prov:End; prov:entity :buzzer; :foo :bar; prov:atTime '2012-03-09T08:05:08-05:00'^^xsd:dateTime ].

per_entity.label: EntityInfluence
per_entity.definition: EntityInfluence provides additional descriptions of an Entity's binary influence upon any other kind of resource. Instances of EntityInfluence use the prov:entity property to cite the influencing Entity.

per_entity.label: Generation
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Generation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasGeneratedBy relation from a generated prov:Entity to the prov:Activity that generated it. For example, :cake prov:wasGeneratedBy :baking; prov:qualifiedGeneration [ a prov:Generation; prov:activity :baking; :foo :bar ].

per_entity.label: Influence
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Influence provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasInfluencedBy relation from some influenced Activity, Entity, or Agent to the influencing Activity, Entity, or Agent. For example, :stomach_ache prov:wasInfluencedBy :spoon; prov:qualifiedInfluence [ a prov:Influence; prov:entity :spoon; :foo :bar ] . Because prov:Influence is a broad relation, the more specific relations (Communication, Delegation, End, etc.) should be used when applicable.

per_entity.label: InstantaneousEvent
per_entity.definition: An instantaneous event, or event for short, happens in the world and marks a change in the world, in its activities and in its entities. The term 'event' is commonly used in process algebra with a similar meaning. Events represent communications or interactions; they are assumed to be atomic and instantaneous.

per_entity.label: Invalidation
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Invalidation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasInvalidatedBy relation from an invalidated prov:Entity to the prov:Activity that invalidated it. For example, :uncracked_egg prov:wasInvalidatedBy :baking; prov:qualifiedInvalidation [ a prov:Invalidation; prov:activity :baking; :foo :bar ].

per_entity.label: Plan
per_entity.definition: There exist no prescriptive requirement on the nature of plans, their representation, the actions or steps they consist of, or their intended goals. Since plans may evolve over time, it may become necessary to track their provenance, so plans themselves are entities. Representing the plan explicitly in the provenance can be useful for various tasks: for example, to validate the execution as represented in the provenance record, to manage expectation failures, or to provide explanations.

per_entity.label: PrimarySource
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:PrimarySource provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:hadPrimarySource relation from some secondary prov:Entity to an earlier, primary prov:Entity. For example, :blog prov:hadPrimarySource :newsArticle; prov:qualifiedPrimarySource [ a prov:PrimarySource; prov:entity :newsArticle; :foo :bar ] .

per_entity.label: Quotation
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Quotation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasQuotedFrom relation from some taken prov:Entity from an earlier, larger prov:Entity. For example, :here_is_looking_at_you_kid prov:wasQuotedFrom :casablanca_script; prov:qualifiedQuotation [ a prov:Quotation; prov:entity :casablanca_script; :foo :bar ].

per_entity.label: Revision
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Revision provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasRevisionOf relation from some newer prov:Entity to an earlier prov:Entity. For example, :draft_2 prov:wasRevisionOf :draft_1; prov:qualifiedRevision [ a prov:Revision; prov:entity :draft_1; :foo :bar ].

per_entity.label: Start
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Start provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasStartedBy relation from some started prov:Activity to an prov:Entity that started it. For example, :foot_race prov:wasStartedBy :bang; prov:qualifiedStart [ a prov:Start; prov:entity :bang; :foo :bar; prov:atTime '2012-03-09T08:05:08-05:00'^^xsd:dateTime ] .

per_entity.label: Usage
per_entity.definition: An instance of prov:Usage provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:used relation from some prov:Activity to an prov:Entity that it used. For example, :keynote prov:used :podium; prov:qualifiedUsage [ a prov:Usage; prov:entity :podium; :foo :bar ].

items.name: Defining multiple domains or ranges in properties
items.description: The domain or range (or both) of a property (relationships and attributes) is defined by stating more than one rdfs:domain or rdfs:range statements. In OWL multiple rdfs:domain or rdfs:range axioms are allowed, but they are interpreted as conjunction, being, therefore, equivalent to the construct owl:intersectionOf. This pitfall is related to the common error that appears when defining domains and ranges described in [7].

items.name: Missing domain or range in properties
items.description: Object and/or datatype properties without domain or range (or none of them) are included in the ontology.

items.name: Inverse relationships not explicitly declared
items.description: This pitfall appears when any relationship (except for those that are defined as symmetric properties using owl:SymmetricProperty) does not have an inverse relationship (owl:inverseOf) defined within the ontology.

rules.title: Ontology has no title
rules.description: Add dcterms:title (or rdfs:label) to the owl:Ontology node.

rules.title: Ontology has no description
rules.description: Add dcterms:description or dcterms:abstract so readers know what the ontology is for.

rules.title: No license declared
rules.description: Declare a license with dcterms:license so others know how they may reuse the ontology.

rules.title: No version information
rules.description: Add owl:versionInfo and owl:versionIRI to make releases citable and comparable.

rules.title: No creators
rules.description: Credit the authors with dcterms:creator.

rules.title: No preferred prefix/namespace
rules.description: Add vann:preferredNamespacePrefix and vann:preferredNamespaceUri.

rules.title: Term without a label
rules.description: Every term should have a human-readable rdfs:label or skos:prefLabel (OOPS! P08).

rules.title: Term without a definition
rules.description: Every term should have a definition (skos:definition, IAO:0000115 or rdfs:comment) (OOPS! P08).

rules.title: Property without domain
rules.description: Consider declaring rdfs:domain (OOPS! P11). Ignored when the property is used in class axioms.

rules.title: Property without range
rules.description: Consider declaring rdfs:range (OOPS! P11).

rules.title: Cycle in class hierarchy
rules.description: A class is (indirectly) a subclass of itself, which makes the classes equivalent (OOPS! P06).

rules.title: Undeclared term
rules.description: A term in the ontology namespace is used but never declared (no rdf:type) (OOPS! P34/P35).

rules.title: Duplicate labels
rules.description: Two or more terms share the same label, which confuses readers and tools.

rules.title: Multiple labels in one language
rules.description: A term has more than one rdfs:label/skos:prefLabel in the same language.

rules.title: Deprecated term without replacement
rules.description: Deprecated terms should point to their replacement with dcterms:isReplacedBy.

rules.title: Inconsistent naming convention
rules.description: Classes are usually UpperCamelCase and properties lowerCamelCase (OOPS! P22).

rules.title: Class both subclass of and disjoint with another
rules.description: A class that is a subclass of a class it is disjoint with is unsatisfiable.

rules.title: Transitive property used as functional
rules.description: In OWL 2 DL a transitive property cannot be functional or inverse functional.

rules.title: Self-referencing definition
rules.description: A class is declared equivalent to or a subclass of itself (OOPS! P24/P27).

rules.title: Orphan class
rules.description: A class with no superclass, no subclasses and no usage is disconnected from the model.

rules.title: Wrong kind of range
rules.description: Datatype properties must have a datatype range and object properties a class range (OOPS! P31-like).

rules.title: Inverse of itself but not symmetric
rules.description: A property declared as inverse of itself should be declared symmetric instead (OOPS! P25).

rules.title: Missing language tags
rules.description: When some labels carry language tags, all of them should (helps multilingual docs).

rules.title: Term outside the ontology namespace
rules.description: Declared terms that live in other namespaces are documented as external.

rules.title: Multiple domains or ranges
rules.description: Several rdfs:domain (or range) axioms are interpreted as their intersection, which is often not intended (OOPS! P19).
